Add web analytics or a support chat widget to a docs site with one line per provider, and ask readers for consent before anything loads. aiui build adds them to every page (the home page, each docs page and 404.html). Each client-side page change counts as a page view.

A provider takes its main id as a plain value (ga4: G-ABC1234) or a block with more settings. The build checks every id and URL and stops on a bad one. With consent, nothing loads until the reader accepts. A small banner at the bottom of the page offers Decline and Accept, the same size and style, so declining is as easy as accepting. The choice is remembered in the browser's local storage (aiui-consent: granted or denied). The banner uses the site's theme colours in light and dark mode and fits a phone screen. Key Default Meaning required true consent: true is short for this; false loads without asking. banner true false: no built-in banner; your own consent tool decides (below). text, accept, decline an English sentence, Accept, Decline The banner's words. policy, policyLabel none, Privacy policy A link to your privacy page (a site path or URL). Change of mind. Any link to #cookie-settings opens the banner again, for example in the footer: Cookie settings. Declining after accepting reloads the page, so the trackers that were running stop. Your own consent tool. Set banner: false and tell the page the reader's choice from the tool's callback:

Readers whose browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track get no analytics (support chat still loads); respectDoNotTrack: false counts them anyway. aiui dev leaves integrations out so previews are not visits; dev: true under integrations loads them there too.

No inline script is emitted: the settings are a JSON data block and the loader is a file at the site root (/aiui-integrations.js). The build's Content Security Policy adds each provider's hosts per directive by itself (Compiler(config).external_origins() lists them). A tag manager container (gtm) loads whatever tags you add to it, so with gtm the policy is report-only until you add their hosts under site.csp and set it to enforce.
